description.narrative: ICHR är en palestinsk oberoende nationell institution med mandat att verka som en ombudsmannainstitution för mänskliga rättigheter. Stödet syftar till att främja de mänskliga rättigheterna i Palestina genom att: (1) följa upp kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter; (2) stärka ansvarsutkrävande och säkerställa att palestinsk lagstiftning och policyramverk är i enlighet med de mänskliga rättigheterna (3) främja opinionsbildning för mänskliga rättigheter i Palestina; samt (4) stärka Palestinas regionala och internationella samarbete kring de mänskliga rättigheterna. Stödet till ICHR är ett kärnstöd för genomförandet av deras strategiska plan 2023-2025. Det koordineras i ett givarkonsortium där Sverige ingår tillsammans med Schweiz, Nederländerna, Norge, Finland samt Danmark.

The ICHR is a Palestinian independent national institution with a mandate to act as an ombudsman institution for human rights. The current support aims to promote human rights in Palestine by: (1) monitoring human rights violations; (2) strengthen accountability and ensure that Palestinian legislation and policy frameworks are consistent with human rights (3) promote human rights advocacy in Palestine; and (4) strengthen Palestine's regional and international cooperation on human rights. The support to the ICHR is a core support for the implementation of their strategic plan 2023-2025. It is coordinated in a donor consortium in which Sweden participates together with Switzerland, the Netherlands, Norway, Finland and Denmark.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sweden and ICHR regarding funding for the ICHR Strategic Plan 2023-2027

description.narrative:
Some outcomes that can be highlighted during 2025 are:
- Through its Ombudsman function, ICHR received and handled 2,117 complaints during 2025, representing a 37.1% increase compared to 2024. According to the report, this increase was linked to improved access to services, particularly in Gaza following the partial resumption of field activities, as well as increased accessibility for vulnerable groups.
ICHR carried out 1,123 visits to detention centres, rehabilitation facilities and care institutions. These visits contributed to concrete improvements in detention conditions, including the establishment of a 24/7 medical clinic in detention facilities, measures to reduce overcrowding, and the opening of the first women's ward in Hebron Rehabilitation Centre. The Commission also successfully advocated for the installation of surveillance cameras in investigation rooms across the West Bank as a preventive measure against ill-treatment and abuse.
Through legal review and policy advocacy, ICHR reviewed 10 draft laws and decree-laws and contributed to a number of institutional responses, including the rescinding of problematic Sharia Court instructions regarding missing persons, government engagement on compulsory lending practices affecting public employees, and interventions that resulted in the release of a detained citizen.
In the area of economic and social rights, ICHR's advocacy contributed to improved access to specialised healthcare for Multiple Sclerosis patients, advanced protection frameworks for unaccompanied and separated children, and renewed policy discussions concerning labour rights and social protection.
Human rights awareness and outreach activities remained extensive despite the challenging context. During the year, ICHR delivered 30 training courses reaching 758 participants, conducted 84 awareness sessions reaching 4,288 participants, and implemented 66 advocacy activities linked to key human rights themes and international observance days.ICHR significantly expanded its digital outreach and public engagement.
The Commission produced more than 1,500 multimedia outputs and generated over 9.3 million views across its social media platforms, substantially increasing the reach of its human rights messaging and public awareness efforts.
At the international level, ICHR strengthened its engagement with UN human rights mechanisms, including treaty bodies, special procedures and the Human Rights Council. Through shadow reports, urgent appeals and strategic advocacy, the Commission contributed to increased international attention to violations of international humanitarian and human rights law and strengthened cooperation with National Human Rights Institutions and international partners.
